title: CORE-03 Multi-Model Fallback Qualification: Secondary Qualified Models & Fallback Routing for Generic Capabilities
purpose: Qualify lfm25-1p2b-thinking-local on core.classify and core.summarize via Benchmark Lab evaluation suites, evidence promotion, and qualification records with canonical checksums to establish secondary qualified fallbacks and activate multi-model shadow routing.
problem: Only a single local model (llama3.2-local) is qualified on generic capabilities. If the primary model fails or is unavailable on edge devices, workflows fail closed without an eligible qualified fallback.

included: Benchmark Lab evaluation of lfm25-1p2b-thinking-local on core-classify-v1 and core-summarize-v1
Evidence promotion and qualification records for lfm25-1p2b-thinking-local on core.classify and core.summarize with canonical checksums
Shadow routing multi-model comparison and fallback recommendation computation
Automated runtime fallback execution in tool-router and run-plan-executor with fallback Track Run Records
excluded: Modifying existing completed Lighthouse, DealSniper, or llama3.2 qualification evidence

acceptanceCriteria.description: Benchmark Lab suite core-classify-v1 evaluates lfm25-1p2b-thinking-local, passes semantic evaluation across strata, and generates approved evidence.
Benchmark Lab suite core-summarize-v1 evaluates lfm25-1p2b-thinking-local, passes semantic evaluation across strata, and generates approved evidence.
Qualification records for lfm25-1p2b-thinking-local with canonical checksums are loaded into Local Brain for core.classify and core.summarize.
Shadow router computes recommendations with valid fallback recommendation when multiple qualified models exist.
Execution automatically falls back to secondary qualified model when primary fails, emitting Track Run Records with fallback metadata.
All existing repository validation commands (npm run test:full) remain 100% green.
